title: Responder Canvas and Exercise Framework
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document provides an operational canvas for responders: a single reference that combines incident classification, concise triage checklists, escalation timing, an embeddable postmortem template, on-call rotation rules, and a repeatable game-day exercise plan. It is intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, and customer success so that incidents are resolved quickly with consistent communications and clear learning loops.

Purpose and scope
------------------
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detection and mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR) by standardizing decisions and communications during production incidents.
- Scope: All customer-impacting incidents across Redwood-hosted services (API gateway, runtime, model-serving pool, storage, and auth). Private deployments should adapt this canvas to their network/CDN specifics.

High-level incident lifecycle (text diagram)
------------------------------------------
1) Signal -> 2) Triage -> 3) Contain -> 4) Recovery -> 5) Notify & Escalate -> 6) Postmortem & Actions
(Observability signals: SLO alerts, error-rate spikes, customer tickets, automated canary alarms.)

Severity classifications and SLAs
--------------------------------
- Sev 1 (TOTAL OUTAGE): Broad customer impact or >50% request failure rate on critical endpoints. Target initial response: 5 minutes. Target MTTR: 1 hour (business hours) for partial restore.
- Sev 2 (DEGRADED): Significant latency or error-rate increase affecting a subset of customers. Initial response: 15 minutes. Target MTTR: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (FEATURE IMPACT): Non-critical feature broken or small subset of customers affected. Initial response: 60 minutes.
- Sev 4 (NO CUSTOMER IMPACT): Internal issues or planned maintenance. Triage during normal hours.

SLOs referenced during triage
----------------------------
- API request success: 99.95% (7d rolling)
- p95 latency for /v1/generate: <= 750ms
- Model-serving GPU OOMs: < 0.5% of jobs per day
If an alert indicates an SLO breach for two consecutive evaluation windows (5m windows), escalate to Sev 2+ immediately.

Roles & responsibilities (quick lookup)
---------------------------------------
- Incident Lead (IL): drives the timeline, decisions, and postmortem. (Default: on-call SRE for the affected service.)
- Primary Responder / Pager: first engineer paged; executes triage checklist.
- Triage Support: on-call infra or runtime engineer for kernel/driver/hosting issues.
- Communications Lead: owns external/internal updates and status page entries (Customer Success or assigned SRE).
- Service Owner: provides context on feature flags, recent deploys, and rollback authority.

Contact channels and tools
--------------------------
- Primary comms: #incident-redwood Slack channel (auto-created by incidentbot).
- Pager system: PagerDuty (PD escalation policy: 3 escalations, 1 minute retry window).
- Teleconference: auto-join link generated by incidentbot ("Join Incident Bridge").
- Status page: status.redwood.ai (internal editor access for Communications Lead).

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------
1) Confirm signal: check alerts dashboard and recent deploys (CI/CD → last 60 minutes).
   - CLI: curl -s https://internal-monitoring/api/alerts?service=api | jq '.recent[] | {alert,level,time}'
2) Identify blast radius: which endpoints/customers/regions are impacted?
   - Query: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND region = 'us-west' GROUP BY customer_id LIMIT 10
3) Verify whether it's config/deployment: rollback window? If a deploy in last 15 minutes, pin to rollback hypothesis.
4) Collect logs and traces: open traces for p99 requests and KV-cache metrics for hot keys.
5) Stabilize traffic: enable rate limits, route traffic away from affected region or use degraded routing policy.
   - Kibana/Logs queries and routing CLI are included in the appendix.

Containment recipes (short actionable steps)
--------------------------------------------
- High error-rate (API 5xx spike):
  1) Toggle out model-variant weight in the routing policy to fallback smaller model: /ops/routing/set-weight --service runtime --variant small-v1 --weight 90
  2) Temporarily enable caching for repeat requests at edge: edge-cli cache enable --pattern '/v1/embeddings' --ttl 60
  3) If errors originate from one cluster, mark it as draining and shift traffic via SmartRouter.
- High-latency across model-serving:
  1) Drain long-running GPU queues: runtime-cli drain --pool g4-pool --grace 120
  2) Increase small-instance autoscale target by +30% (if burst budget allows).
- GPU OOMs or model memory faults:
  1) Drop quantization-unfriendly models to a lower-seq-length configuration.
  2) Pin new model variants to CPU (if supported) while recovering GPU pool.

Escalation timing (quick matrix)
--------------------------------
- After 15 minutes (Sev 1): IL calls CTO-on-call and notifies legal if SLA risk present.
- After 60 minutes (Sev 1): invoke cross-functional war room (SRE, runtime, infra, customer-success, PR).
- For Sev 2: after 4 hours, prepare formal customer update and executive summary.

Status page & customer comms templates
-------------------------------------
(Communications Lead should adapt tone based on severity.)

- Initial customer notification (Sev 1) - Subject: "[Incident] Degraded API availability - We are investigating"
  Body (short):
  "Status: Investigating
   Impact: Some API requests are failing for customers in US-West and EU.
   Mitigation: We have routed traffic away from the affected cluster and are rolling back a recent runtime deploy.
   Next update: 15 minutes or sooner.
   Reference: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/XXXX"

- Progress update - Subject: "[Update] Incident XXXX — mitigation in progress"
  Body:
  "Update: Error rates have decreased from 76% -> 21% for impacted endpoints. We continue to validate the rollback and run validation prompts.
   ETA for recovery: ~30 minutes.
   Actions taken: rollback deploy, disabled routing variant 'canary-2025-09', increased cache TTL."

- Resolution notice - Subject: "[Resolved] Incident XXXX — API service restored"
  Body:
  "We have restored full service and verified successful request rates for affected endpoints. Root cause analysis is in progress; a post-incident summary will be published within 72 hours. If you see continued issues, please open a support ticket or reply to this message."

Postmortem template (use as checklist)
-------------------------------------
- Title and incident ID
- Severity and start/end times (UTC)
- Summary (1-2 paragraphs)
- Impact: customers affected, % of requests, regions, customers (anonymized)
- Timeline (concise bullet timeline with timestamps and owner initials)
- Root cause statement (single sentence)
- Contributing factors (3–6 bullets)
- Corrective actions (short term and long term), with owner and ETA (owner format: LastnameInitial, e.g. PatelA)
- Rollback/mitigation steps executed and validation evidence (links to dashboards/traces)
- Severity review and prevention checklist
- Lessons learned and follow-ups (tracked in the incident backlog)

Incident backlog and action tracking
----------------------------------
- Create a Jira ticket for each corrective action with label incident-XXXX and link back to postmortem.
- All action owners are expected to provide status at weekly incident review until action is closed.

On-call rotation rules and handover checklist
--------------------------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week for SREs, 2 weeks for platform leads.
- Handover window: outgoing engineer posts 30-minute overlap note summarizing known issues, current alerts, and scheduled maintenance.
- Escalation responsibilities: if pager unacknowledged after 5 minutes escalate to secondary, after 15 minutes page IL.
- Shadowing: new hires shadow three rotations before being primary on-call.

Game day exercise blueprint (quarterly cadence)
---------------------------------------------
Purpose: Validate detection, paging, communications, rollback, and postmortem workflow under controlled conditions.
Duration: 2 hours (1-hour incident, 1-hour debrief).
Participants: 2 SREs on-call, 1 runtime engineer, 1 infra, 1 customer success, 1 engineering manager.
Scenario examples:
- Simulated p95 latency spike caused by KV cache stampede.
- Model-serving cluster unavailable after driver update.
- Canary causing 40% elevated error-rate for a subset of customers.

Pre-game checklist:
1) Define blast radius and which metrics will be used for assertion.
2) Create a synthetic traffic load (locust/jitter harness) tagged game-day-YYYYMM.
3) Notify status.redwood.ai in draft mode and set internal-only flag.
4) Prepare rollback knobs and test access.

During the exercise:
- Timebox actions; the IL must call time at 20-minute intervals.
- Communications Lead practices status updates using template above.
- Validate that PD alert triggers Slack channel and bridge auto-joins.

Post-game debrief
----------------
- Publish a short retrospective: what worked, what did not, 3 immediate follow-ups.
- Convert follow-ups into Jira with priority P2 and link to game-day doc.

Appendix: example CLI snippets and dashboard links
------------------------------------------------
- List recent deploys (internal CLI):
  $ releases-cli list --service runtime --since 60m
- Open hot traces for a request id:
  $ traces-cli open --request-id 67a4f2b
- Force a lightweight rollback:
  $ deploy-cli rollback --service runtime --to-tag tags/release-2025-08-10 --reason "automatic rollback during incident"

- Dashboards (internal links):
  - Alerts: https://internal-monitoring/dashboards/alerts
  - Runtime metrics: https://internal-monitoring/dashboards/runtime-p95
  - Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/editor

Appendix B: quick sample postmortem (shortened)
------------------------------------------------
Title: API error storm — incident-2025-07-04
Severity: Sev 1
Start: 2025-07-04T10:12:00Z End: 2025-07-04T12:05:00Z
Summary: A faulty routing variant from a canary deploy caused 5xx for a subset of requests. We rolled back the canary and restored service; partial validation took an additional 50 minutes.
Root cause: a runtime networking regression introduced in the canary image.
Actions: pin canary, add pre-rollout network probing, add alert for rapid-deploy-failure-pattern. Owner: ChenM ETA: 2025-08-01

Related links and references
---------------------------
- Incident automation repo: git.redwood.ai/ops/incidentbot
- Incident classification decision record: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/incident-classification-2024
- Runbook library: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks

How to use this canvas
----------------------
1) Bookmark this page and the postmortem template before starting an incident.
2) Use the triage checklist in the first 10 minutes and assign IL.
3) If a template field is blank, prefer conservative communications (more frequent updates).
4) After resolution, publish postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and the final within 7 days.

Owners and maintenance
----------------------
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (SRE Lead)
- Review cadence: annual or after any Sev 1 event.
- Next scheduled review: 2026-02-01

Feedback and improvement
------------------------
Send suggestions or proposed edits via PR to the confluence page or open an issue in git.redwood.ai/ops/incident-improvements with label 'inc-canvas'.
